targets.name: Barnard's Star
targets.note: Fastest known stellar proper motion: about 10 arcsec a year, 1.7 SPHEREx pixels. Try Difference: the star leaves a dark and a bright half.

targets.name: WISE 0855-0714
targets.source: Position from the challenge statement; motion from Luhman (2014)
targets.note: Coldest known brown dwarf. Visible to SPHEREx only at 4-5 um; switch to detector 5 or 6.

targets.name: Epsilon Indi B
targets.note: A pair of nearby brown dwarfs seen as one source. SPHEREx measures its motion to within 0.1 arcsec of Gaia.

targets.name: RW Aurigae
targets.source: AAVSO VSX (OID 3777): classical T Tauri star, irregular
targets.note: Young star with irregular dimming. Its infrared glow faded by 0.5-0.75 mag between September 2025 and September 2026.

targets.name: R Draconis
targets.source: AAVSO VSX (OID 13673): Mira, period 246.12 d, V 6.7-13.2
targets.note: Mira variable in SPHEREx's northern deep field: 2,589 exposures follow its 246-day pulsation.

targets.name: Makemake
targets.note: Dwarf planet about 52 au away. Turn the distance focus and it snaps into a point.

targets.name: Haumea
targets.note: Dwarf planet about 49 au away, on a nearly circular orbit: the cleanest control.

targets.name: Pluto
targets.note: About 35 au away on an eccentric orbit, where the circular-orbit assumption is weakest.

targets.name: Eris
targets.note: About 95 au away and faint: near the limit of what single exposures can show.
